2.0.s.en: 1. Those who came up from the captivity

2.0.0.en: 1 Now these are the children of the province that went up out of the captivity, of those which had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon, and came again unto Jerusalem and Judah, every one unto his city; 2 Which came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mizpar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah. 2.0.1.en: Now these are the children of the province that went up out of the captivity, of those which had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon, and came again unto Jerusalem and Judah, every one unto his city [1].

2.0.2.en: By "province" is meant here Judah, which was formerly a great kingdom with dependencies; it had become merely a province, that is, a district subject to the king of Persia. This is the work of sin, which humbles man as it does nations and kingdoms. Evil has been linked with disgrace, shame and the loss of peace, together with failure and inner defeat, and righteousness with true dignity. The wicked man does not need anyone to restrain and punish him; rather, what he does brings him bitterness and death! He drinks from the very cup that he has filled for himself, unless he throws the cup away through his enjoyment of fellowship with his Savior and his earnest striving through the holy will in the Lord.

2.0.3.en: "Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people" (Prov 14:34).

2.0.4.en: "When the wicked cometh, then cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach" (Prov 18:3).

2.0.5.en: "Whenever they served a god other than their own, they were handed over to plunder, the sword and shame" (Jdt 5:18).

2.0.6.en: "Let them be confounded and consumed that are adversaries to my soul; let them be covered with reproach and dishonour that seek my hurt" (Ps 71:13).

2.0.7.en: "There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked" (Isa 48:22).

2.0.8.en: "Do not become an enemy after being a friend, for a bad name inherits shame and reproach; so too the sinner who is double-tongued" (Sir 6:1).

2.0.9.en: "Lying is a foul disgrace in a man, and it is ever in the mouths of the undisciplined" (Sir 20:26).

2.0.10.en: * If you remain in what belongs to the dust, you will in the end be changed into it. It befits you to change, you must be transformed, you must become heavenly.

2.0.11.en: Origen * Since I am blamed for every fold of my sins, I spend my days and nights in terror; but when I see God loosing the bonds and upholding the humble, terrified soul, He says to me as I lie prostrate in the tomb of my wickedness: [Jerome, come forth].

2.0.12.en: St. Jerome * These wicked men head toward killing themselves with every kind of lust... Yes, even when they live they are in shame, for they count their bellies as their gods, and when they die they are tormented.

2.0.13.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic Those who came with Zerubbabel:

2.0.14.en: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mizpar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah.

2.1.0.en: The number of the men of the people of Israel [2].

2.1.1.en: Since those who returned to Jerusalem accepted leaving much behind and enduring hardships and dangers for the sake of building the city of God, Jerusalem, and His temple, God honored them by mentioning their names. "For them that honour me I will honour" (1 Sam 2:30). God preserves the names of those who fear Him, for "the memory of the just is blessed" (Prov 10:7), and He honors them in this world as in the age to come.

2.1.2.en: The names of those who work for the Kingdom of God are recorded, so that they may also be recorded in the book of eternal life (Rev 3:5).

2.1.3.en: This register did not mention all the names, being content at times with the names of the heads of the houses and clans, and at times with the number only. But as for those who fear the Lord, their names are recorded with the Lord in the book of remembrance (Mal 3:16-17).

2.1.4.en: * ["The memory of the just is praised"](*). He did not say this to mean that departed souls are helped by our praise. Rather, he said this because those who praise the departed receive the greatest benefit from remembering them; therefore, since we receive much benefit from their holy remembrance, let us not despise the words of the wise man, but rather give heed to them.

2.1.5.en: St. John Chrysostom Nehemiah here is not the Nehemiah, the leader of the third company, who rebuilt the wall about 80 years later; likewise Mordecai here is not the Mordecai mentioned in the Book of Esther.

2.12.1.en: "Adonikam" means "the great lord." We note that the number 666 is the number of the beast (Rev 13), that is, Satan. It is as though with every return to God we should expect warfare from the enemy of good, as long as we are still in the flesh.

2.22.0.en: The men of Anathoth, an hundred twenty and eight [23].

2.22.1.en: The men of Anathoth [23]: they were the people of the village of the prophet Jeremiah, who accused him of treason and abandoned him. Jeremiah prophesied about the return from captivity while he was in prison, where King Zedekiah had confined him on the charge that he was an agent of Nebuchadnezzar. His cousin Hanameel came to him that he might buy from him his field that was in Anathoth, even though he knew that the Chaldeans would seize the land. He bought the field, wrote the deed and called witnesses, and commanded Baruch to put it in an earthen vessel, as a testimony that after the devastation of the land, life would return to it (Jer 32:43-43). Behold, God's promise has been fulfilled and the captives have returned, and the men of Anathoth have returned to rebuild the land.

2.24.0.en: The children of Kirjath-arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty and three [25].

2.30.1.en: "The other Elam" is so called to distinguish it from the Elam mentioned in verse 7; the first is the name of a person, whereas here it is the name of a place.

2.35.0.en: The priests: the children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy and three [36].

2.35.1.en: We expected all the priests to return, but sadly only groups from four divisions returned, and the rest preferred work in the land of captivity and its enterprises to the house of the Lord.

2.35.2.en: "Jeshua" mentioned here is not the one mentioned in (v. 2).

2.35.3.en: It is noted that the total number of the priests is about 4,200, about a tenth of those who returned to Jerusalem, as though God wished to keep the tithes for Himself.

2.39.1.en: It is noted that the number of the Levites is very small, perhaps because they rejected their office and made light of it, since they wanted to have land and possessions, forgetting that the Lord is their portion and that they are the Lord's portion.

2.58.s.en: 2. Those whose genealogies could not be established

2.58.0.en: 59 And these were they which went up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsa, Cherub, Addan, Immer: but they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel: 60 The children of Delaiah, the children of Tobiah, the children of Nekoda, six hundred fifty and two. 61 And of the children of the priests: the children of Habaiah, the children of Koz, the children of Barzillai; which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name: 62 These sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood. 63 And the Tirshatha said unto them, that they should not eat of the most holy things, till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim. 64 The whole congregation together was forty and two thousand three hundred and threescore, 65 Beside their servants and their maids, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred thirty and seven: and there were among them two hundred singing men and singing women. 66 Their horses were seven hundred thirty and six; their mules, two hundred forty and five; 67 Their camels, four hundred thirty and five; their asses, six thousand seven hundred and twenty.

2.58.1.en: And these were they which went up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsa, Cherub, Addan, Immer.

2.58.2.en: But they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel [59].

2.58.3.en: Genealogical registers were of great importance to the Hebrews, especially for the priests and the Levites. Whoever could not prove that he was of the seed of Abraham was deprived of certain special privileges.

2.58.4.en: It is shameful that some of the returnees, because of their love of money, lost interest in proving their fathers' houses [59].

2.58.5.en: "They could not shew their father's house": these were Israelites, but they had lost their lists of descent. Among them were priests, who were required to be of the seed of Aaron.

2.59.0.en: The children of Delaiah, the children of Tobiah, the children of Nekoda, six hundred fifty and two [60].

2.59.1.en: "Delaiah" means "whom Jehovah has freed." "Tobiah" means "the goodness of Jehovah." And "Nekoda" means "famous." Although these names carry beautiful spiritual meanings, they could not prove their descent from the people of God, perhaps because their fathers had married pagan women. These were counted as circumcised strangers who have the right to worship and to offer sacrifices (Num 15:14-16), but have no portion in the land.

2.60.0.en: And of the children of the priests: the children of Habaiah, the children of Koz, the children of Barzillai; which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name [61].

2.60.1.en: Some of the priests changed their descent to Barzillai the Gileadite instead of tracing it to the tribe of Aaron [61], so they were forbidden to eat of the most holy things, that is, from their portions as priests, and were given only the holy things, which are the portions of the families of the priests [61-63]. Many of the people, even those of Gentile origin, went before the priests and entered the procession, and became heroes before the Lord. Some of the people go before the priests in the heavenly glories. "The children of Barzillai": these lost the priesthood, for they lost the worthiness for it. Their father was a priest, yet he preferred to be called by the name of a famous man, Barzillai the Gileadite, and abandoned his descent from Aaron. He did not realize the dignity of the priesthood and the service of God, so he rejected his priestly lineage. Whoever denies the Son of Man, the Son of Man also denies him.

2.61.0.en: These sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood [62].

2.62.0.en: And the Tirshatha said unto them, that they should not eat of the most holy things, till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim [63].

2.62.1.en: These who were rejected from the priesthood deprived themselves of the showbread and of sharing in the flesh of the holy sacrifice and the drink offering, which only the priests eat and which is figuratively called the most holy. As for the firstfruits, the thank offerings and the tithes, the whole house of the priest eats them, and they are called the holy things.

2.62.2.en: Tirshatha: a Persian word referring to the governor, and it may mean a title of respect such as "His Excellency so-and-so." The governor here is Zerubbabel.

2.62.3.en: "A priest with Urim and Thummim": these were two flat stones on the breastplate of the high priest, called the "breastplate of judgment" (Ex 28:30; Lev 8:8), through which God answers his questions; they signify submission to God's will in the matters concerning the people as a whole.

2.62.4.en: The word "Urim" means "the lights," and "Thummim" means "completion" or "perfections."

2.62.5.en: Here we find an indication of Israel's waiting for the coming of the High Priest in whom are all the lights and perfections, that is, the Lord Christ.

2.62.6.en: In any case, the "Urim and Thummim" affirm that in the life of the priest, he must not depend in his ministry on human arms and human counsels, but first take refuge at the altar, where he pours himself out before God, asking that His divine light shine in his heart and complete every weakness in him. For the priest's many, grave and intricate obligations, since he undertakes to guide people in the most precious thing they have, the salvation of their souls, and deals with different kinds of people under varying circumstances, make him need to be in continual contact with God his guide, lest a soul perish because of his ignorance or his inability to do the work.

2.62.7.en: * The Lord Himself is the one who works, and He is the one who offers all.

2.63.0.en: St. John Chrysostom The whole congregation together was forty and two thousand three hundred and threescore [64]. Beside their servants and their maids, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred thirty and seven: and there were among them two hundred singing men and singing women [65].

2.63.1.en: He mentions the total of the multitudes, without the servants and maids, as 42,360, as stated in the Book of Nehemiah, whereas the total of the numbers given here is 29,818, and the total of the numbers given in Nehemiah is 31,089. What is the reason for this? 1. The number 42,360 is the number of the notable Jews who wished to return, and this number is constant in Ezra and Nehemiah. But those whom Ezra mentions are those who set out to return and wrote their names while in Babylon, whereas Nehemiah wrote them while in Judea after the walls of Jerusalem were built. A difference arose because of the long interval between them; some must have died on the journey, and some after arriving, before Nehemiah recorded the names. Some also changed their minds about traveling, so their names dropped out of the seventh chapter of the Book of Nehemiah. 2. After Ezra recorded the names of those who set out on the journey, others also traveled, and Nehemiah recorded them, so Nehemiah's list increased.

2.63.2.en: Examples of this: 1. Magbish is not mentioned in Nehemiah's list, but he is mentioned in (Ezra 2:30). Although Ezra, in Babylon, recorded his name, Nehemiah gave the names of those who had actually arrived in Jerusalem. 2. The children of Adin number 454 in Ezra's list, and their number in Nehemiah's list is 655, because those who actually traveled were more than those who registered their names. 3. It was the custom of the Jews at that time to use more than one name, and this custom still exists in Upper Egypt to this day. We find that a person's name on the birth certificate differs from the name by which he has been known since his birth, and people often do not know his registered name until he enters school or when he marries and needs to present the birth certificate. Here we find an example: the children of Sia (Neh 7:47) are the children of Siaha in (Ezra 2:44).

2.63.3.en: "The singing men and singing women" here are not of the Levites who praise God in the temple, but those who hold entertainments and banquets.

2.63.4.en: Their horses were seven hundred thirty and six.

2.64.0.en: Their mules, two hundred forty and five [66].

2.64.1.en: Their camels, four hundred thirty and five.

2.65.0.en: Their asses, six thousand seven hundred and twenty [67].

2.65.1.en: These went into captivity with nothing, and returned with horses, camels, servants, gold and silver. These are gifts of God that He gives to the person who accepts discipline with thanksgiving, in earnest, and cares for the salvation of his soul; his Savior does not leave him empty.

2.66.0.en: 68 And some of the chief of the fathers, when they came to the house of the LORD which is at Jerusalem, offered freely for the house of the LORD to set it up in his place: 69 They gave after their ability unto the treasure of the work threescore and one thousand drams of gold, and five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priests' garments. 70 So the priests, and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinims, dwelt in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

2.66.1.en: And some of the chief of the fathers, when they came to the house of the LORD which is at Jerusalem, offered freely for the house of the LORD to set it up in his place [68].

2.66.2.en: These gave freely for the temple of the Lord; therefore the Lord blessed them.

2.66.3.en: No one dared to change the place of the temple; rather, the temple of Zerubbabel was built on the same site where the temple of Solomon had been built. To this day the Jews still hope to build the temple on the same site, which causes problems with the Palestinians that are hard, and perhaps even impossible, to solve.

2.67.0.en: They gave after their ability unto the treasure of the work threescore and one thousand drams of gold, and five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priests' garments [69].

2.67.1.en: All shared in leaving Babylon with its glories, and came to Jerusalem, which had become a ruin, burned with fire. Perhaps all paid the tithes. This is the first mile; the second mile is the presenting of gifts and offerings to the house of the Lord, each according to his ability. As the Apostle says: "For to their power, I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they gave of their own accord" (2 Cor 8:3).

2.67.2.en: * This is the height of praise, for in sorrows they remain in peace, and in the depths of poverty they give generously of what they have.

2.67.3.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus The dram is a coin used in the kingdom of Persia. Here is the first mention of minted coins in the Bible.

2.67.4.en: Those who returned from the captivity gave garments for the priests, which they wear at the time of service and take off after finishing the service, keeping them in the treasury of the temple (Ex 28:41; 31:10). They gave them to motivate the priests to begin the service immediately after the return.

2.67.5.en: Mina: the name of a standard for what is weighed, and not the name of a minted coin, and its value is estimated at about 50 shekels.

2.68.0.en: So the priests, and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinims, dwelt in their cities, and all Israel in their cities [70].

2.68.1.en: They returned to their dwellings singing their psalms: "Lord, thou hast been favourable unto thy land..." (Ps 85:1-3). So it befits us to return to our heavenly city, and for our hearts not to be bound to the land of our exile in this world.

2.68.2.en: Gather me into Your joyful procession!

2.68.3.en: * If my sins have driven me into captivity, You are the Liberator of souls from the captivity of the devil, and their Deliverer from slavery.

2.68.4.en: Who can free me from the enemy of good but You?

2.68.5.en: Who will restore to me the dignity of the glory of the children of God that You granted me?

2.68.6.en: Who will gather me into Your rejoicing procession but Your grace!

2.68.7.en: * Draw me and all my brothers in humanity after You.

2.68.8.en: That the souls of all may rejoice in the overflow of Your love.

2.68.9.en: That we may join the procession of victory heading to the Jerusalem above, and our life be turned into a rejoicing heaven.

2.68.10.en: And that the names of all may be recorded in Your book, and You engrave them on Your divine palm.

2.68.11.en: * May You gather all to Yourself: priests and people.

2.68.12.en: May You gather the children and the elders with the young men, the men and the women.

2.68.13.en: May all find a place in Your unique procession.

2.68.14.en: * Grant us to offer a little of what You have granted us.

2.68.15.en: We offer You gold, silver and spiritual precious stones!

2.68.16.en: Accept them and smell them as a sweet savor of pleasure and delight!

2.68.17.en: For we long for You to set up Your holy temple within us!

2.68.18.en: And for all humanity, if possible, to be honored living stones!

2.68.19.en: We offer You sacrifices of continual thanksgiving with the hymns of the angels!

2.68.20.en: Glory to You, O loving and wonderful Leader!
